F_LIVE_1.title: Seat revocation closes every durable door and does not detach an already-bound live socket
F_LIVE_1.severityJudgement: It IS a real privacy defect, not a cosmetic one: after the GM's removal commits and the durable seat is stamped revoked, the removed participant continues to receive campaign-scoped committed facts for as long as the socket stays open. The acceptance line names 'revocation' as one of its five cells, and the team's own comment at bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:925-933 states the design intent that durable membership - not connection state - decides admission ('Before this, revocation lasted exactly as long as they stayed disconnected, because the code was the whole check'). The live-delivery half is the mirror residual of that intent. It is bounded, which is why it is medium-high and not high: exposure requires the removed party to hold the socket open, it ends at the next disconnect, and it cannot be re-established (R4 and R5 verified live that both the scoped read and the rejoin are refused across processes and across an OS restart). VERDICT: this slice is APPROVED as evidence with the gap honestly pinned, but R2.authority-live should NOT be marked accepted on its 'revocation' cell until the production fix lands - a privacy acceptance that says 'revocation' should mean the removed seat stops seeing campaign facts, not merely that it stops being able to ask for them.

F_LIVE_2.title: RemoveParticipant is unreachable through the HTTP command route for every caller including the GM
F_LIVE_2.assessment: VERIFIED, and the receipt's refusal to call it a bug is the right call. Both pipeline call sites omit hostPlayerId (:276-281 and :503-508), so the refusal is unconditional across the whole /commands surface, not specific to one arm - a fact the review adds. The receipt's 'UNDETERMINED' framing is correct: GM administration verbs living on the GM's own socket rather than on a bearer-token HTTP route is a defensible design, and nothing read this session states the intent either way.
F_LIVE_2.reviewAddition: The type-level shape is the part worth an owner sentence. 'hostPlayerId?: string' (CampaignMatchHostIntent.ts:130) is OPTIONAL, so the pipeline's omission compiles silently and turns a host-only AUTHORISATION check into an unconditional refusal with no diagnostic anywhere. Whatever the intent, that silence is the smell: either the parameter should be required (forcing every call site to say what it means), or the host-only intents should be split into their own validator arm that the HTTP pipeline cannot reach at all. Fail-closed is the safe direction, so this is a design-clarity item rather than a security one.
F_LIVE_2.useInTheSpec: Correct. Asserting the 422 as a CONTROL row (spec:196-217) rather than asserting it in a comment is what makes the drive's use of the socket a demonstrated necessity, and the head-unchanged assertion at spec:217 closes the obvious alternative reading that the control accidentally committed the removal the later rows read.

Splitting would add two review cycles and two windows in which main carries an unreferenced helper.
